title: OpenDuckFrame | Free Mac frame generation and video upscaling
description: OpenDuckFrame (开源小鸭) is a free, open-source Mac app for real-time video frame interpolation and upscaling. Apple silicon, macOS 14+. Local processing, no account.
ariaHero: OpenDuckFrame Quality Workbench: choose a window, count down, start frame generation
heroSub: OpenDuckFrame is a free, open-source Mac app for real-time frame generation and upscaling. Choose a window, display or local video for smoother, clearer pictures. All picture processing happens on your Mac.
heroCaption: Earlier interface illustration. Press Delayed enhancement, then focus your target window. The default countdown is 3 seconds and can be changed in Settings.
whatBody: OpenDuckFrame is a native Mac image-enhancement app. It detects source cadence and generates intermediate frames with ODF-VFI or Apple interpolation, with independently configurable upscaling. Windows, displays and local video files are supported; pictures stay on your Mac.
f1d: Counts only frames that actually change, so 24 fps video counts as 24 even on a 120 Hz display.
f2d: On supported macOS 26+ devices, new and reset profiles use Apple low latency at 2×. Other devices use ODF-VFI; saved choices are preserved. Apple FRC is also available where supported.
f3d: Supported devices offer Apple low-latency and Apple video super resolution. Scaling is off by default. Live capture requires frame generation off for video SR; large inputs may be reduced first.
f4t: Adjusts the multiplier to the budget
f4d: Live multiplier mode adjusts the effective multiplier to the processing budget. Smoothness still depends on the Mac and input.
f5d: Live multiplier mode lowers the multiplier to fit the display. At 1×, it passes through the original picture.
f6d: A small overlay shows the content rate, the output rate and the current multiplier.
f7d: Capture and models run on your Mac. No account, and the picture never leaves the machine.
insideTitle: Pick by picture, not by parameter
insideSub: The workbench groups source, frame generation, upscaling and output, with a three-step guide. Choose ODF-VFI or Apple interpolation; supported devices also offer Apple low-latency and video super resolution. The image below is the earlier v0.1.0 technology library.

usesTitle: What can you use it on?
usesSub: Choose a window, a display or a local video. Protected content may not be capturable.
c1d: Video sites in the browser, in a normal window or full-page mode.
c2d: Films and series in your player, with pans that no longer judder.
c4d: Render games at a lower resolution for more frames, then upscale to your screen.
c5d: Stream games from a Windows PC and upscale them on the Mac for a sharper picture.
c6d: Old films and low-bitrate video, upscaled to your screen.
usesNote: Pictures and frame-rate values are illustrative. Actual results depend on the Mac, engine and source.
dlBody: Release builds are published on GitHub, together with every earlier version.
reqs: macOS 14 or later · Mac with Apple silicon
s1d: Open the downloaded .dmg and drag OpenDuckFrame into Applications. This community build is not Apple notarized; macOS may block its first launch.
s2d: Window or display capture requires Screen Recording access. Automatically resizing the source window also requires Accessibility access. Local video playback does not need Screen Recording.
s3t: Focus a window during the countdown
s3d: Open File › Quality Workbench, configure enhancement, press Delayed enhancement, then focus your target window. Enhancement starts when the countdown ends. Settings allow 1–20 seconds; the default is 3.
n1: On supported devices, new and reset profiles use Apple low latency at 2×; saved engine choices remain unchanged.
n2: Windows are grouped by application. Refresh guides Screen Recording access and reloads the list when permission becomes available.
n3: A download control appears when an update is available; Apple video super resolution reuses buffers. Results depend on the device and source.
l1: Frame generation adds latency, which varies with engine, resolution and quality settings. Compare original and enhanced output for latency-sensitive use.
l2: Resizing, fullscreen transitions and occlusion can affect source capture. If needed, reselect the source and compare normal window mode.
a1: OpenDuckFrame is a free, MIT-licensed Mac app for frame generation and upscaling. It enhances windows, displays or local video with ODF-VFI, Apple interpolation and Apple super resolution where available.
q2: Which Macs are supported? What about Windows and Intel?
a2: Apple silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later are supported. Apple low latency and Apple super resolution require macOS 26+; Apple FRC requires macOS 15.4+. All depend on runtime support. Apple super resolution requires SDR input and has engine-specific size and factor limits. Intel Macs, Windows, iPhone and iPad are not supported.
a3: Yes. Generating in-between pictures adds latency, which varies with engine, resolution and quality settings. Start with 2× and compare the picture and interaction before and after enhancement; choose carefully for latency-sensitive use.
q4: Does it work in full screen?
a4: Window and display output follow the source, and the mouse remains usable. Switching a source app to native fullscreen can affect capture; compatibility depends on the app and mode. Local video can be played fullscreen on a selected display.
a5: Enhancement runs locally, without automatically uploading captured pictures or media, and no account is required. Update checks use the network. Sending feedback submits the content you enter and any screenshot you explicitly attach.
a6: Free. The project's own code is MIT licensed on GitHub. FFmpeg, RIFE, model weights and other dependencies retain their own licenses.
q7: macOS says it can't verify the developer.
a7: This community build is not Apple notarized. If you trust the download, review its blocked-launch message in System Settings → Privacy & Security and decide whether to allow it. The app does not change system security settings.
q8: How do I generate frames for video on a Mac?
a8: After installing, open File → Quality Workbench and start with 2× frame generation. For a window, press Delayed enhancement and focus the target before the countdown ends. Displays and video files use Start enhancement. Window and display capture need Screen Recording permission.
q9: Does selecting a multiplier guarantee 120 fps?
a9: A multiplier is a requested processing mode, not a guarantee of displayed frame rate. The engine, source cadence, resolution and display refresh rate affect the result. A 60 Hz display cannot present 120 distinct frames per second. Check the FPS overlay and the picture you actually see.
q10: What is the difference between frame generation and upscaling?
a10: Frame generation adds intermediate pictures for smoother motion; upscaling enlarges a picture. Each has separate controls. Live Apple video super resolution requires frame generation to be off. Compare results at the same output size.

openBody: OpenDuckFrame (Chinese name: 开源小鸭) is a free, MIT-licensed Mac desktop app. It generates in-between frames for existing video and offers independent upscaling. Picture processing runs locally.

q11: Can an upgrade ask for permission again?
a11: Yes. This community build is ad-hoc signed, so macOS may ask for Screen Recording or Accessibility access again after an upgrade. Follow the system prompt in Privacy & Security. Ordinary local video playback does not need Screen Recording permission.
